title: Human-Centered Design of Video-Based Health Education: An Iterative, Collaborative, Community-Based Approach
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how to design and disseminate scalable video-based health education so that it is accessible, engaging, culturally relevant, and adaptable across learner groups and delivery platforms. Rather than evaluating a single intervention effect, the paper synthesizes five years of experience creating and distributing multiple video-based health education initiatives and uses those projects to derive practical design guidelines.

The core approach is human-centered design (HCD) combined with community-based collaboration. The authors describe iterative development processes that included local stakeholders, community members, and end users; rapid prototyping; feedback via WhatsApp, Google Drive, videoconferencing, and in-person bodystorming; and the use of narratives, local voices, celebrity role models, and simplified visuals to improve identification and resonance. Examples span undergraduate medical/health education, international online courses, and community health education in South Africa and other settings.

The paper argues that participatory design increases ownership, engagement, and the likelihood that content will be understandable and reusable across contexts. It also emphasizes tradeoffs between realism and adaptability: live footage may improve authenticity but increases file size and reduces ease of localization, whereas simpler icon-based or illustrated formats are easier to scale and translate. The main conclusion is that HCD can help create durable, scalable educational media whose effectiveness and reach depend heavily on implementation conditions such as audience fit, localization, and platform constraints.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a tutorial/design paper rather than an empirical evaluation. It presents implementation guidelines and illustrative case examples, but no primary outcome data, comparison group, or causal design is reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper offers potentially useful implementation guidance for scalable educational video design, especially around adaptation and community engagement, but it does not report measured effects. Impact is therefore unclear and based on conceptual relevance rather than demonstrated outcomes.

interventions.use_case: human-centered design guidance for creating and disseminating video-based health education content, including collaborative scripting, rapid iteration, community voiceovers, and mobile/tablet delivery
